jobs.title: Software Engineer, Telematics
jobs.description_text: We are looking for an experienced backend software engineer to join our Road Safety & Telematics team. At Lyft, Telematics data is used to make Lyft safer by reducing the frequency and severity of accidents, which in turn also makes Lyft more affordable for riders and a better way to earn a living for drivers. The Telematics team acts as a platform team that processes petabytes of mobile sensor data — millisecond-level IMU, gyroscope, and GPS signals — through a series of DAG-based transformations and ML model inferences to detect harsh driving events and convert them into normalized risk features that other Lyft services consume. Our technology stack runs on AWS, Kubernetes, Spark, and Apache Airflow. In this role, you'll work closely with data scientists, actuarial teams, other backend and data engineers, and product management — partnering across geos to build risk-aware products that rank and reward safe drivers, help off-board unsafe ones, notify drivers in real time, and give claims agents the tools to understand exactly what happened in a ride. You'll also be a key technical partner to our insurance team as they optimize coverage costs and provider relationships. If you are a seasoned engineer with a passion for innovation, high-volume data pipelines, microservices, working in cross-disciplinary environments and possess the skills to ensure the ongoing maintenance and improvement of services, you will thrive on our team! Work with operations and software teams to define protocols for nominal and off-nominal situations (e.g., severe weather response, sensor degradation, connectivity outages, and trip interruptions). Create processes for ongoing field safety monitoring and support the establishment of leading and lagging safety indicators and tooling needed. Analyze operational trends and past field events to drive systemic safety enhancements across both development and operations. Support the Operations team in developing and executing incident response training and operational preparedness activities. Interface with regulatory bodies and contribute to industry standards discussions around AV operational safety validation approaches. Qualifications: Undergrad in Robotics, Mechanical Engine

jobs.title: Staff Systems Engineer - Safety Methodologies
jobs.description_text: To learn more visit: www.waabi.ai At the heart of our mission is an unwavering commitment to safety. We are seeking a passionate and experienced safety or systems engineer to spearhead the development and implementation of critical safety framework methods that underpin our driverless autonomy readiness decisions. This is a unique opportunity to shape how Waabi quantitatively ensures and validates the safety of our autonomous trucking solution, working with our highly realistic simulator, real-world data, and cutting-edge generative AI techniques. You will play a pivotal role in creating the evidence for safe operation and leading efforts in a rapidly evolving and groundbreaking field. You will... Inform driverless release testing by developing sample-efficient, high-signal safety datasets across simulation and closed-course track testing. Establish and manage a robust feedback loop from on-road monitoring and safety relevant events to continuously expand and refine test coverage. Validate and optimize safety evaluation pipelines by conducting comparative analyses on core safety frameworks and benchmark criteria to continuously evolve our safety frameworks. Own the creation of clear and structured safety artifacts, ensuring all readiness decisions are transparent and fully traceable to validation evidence. Mentor peers by fostering a culture of technical excellence and driving clear, constructive collaboration between teams. Qualifications: Undergrad required; Masters or PhD

jobs.title: 車両テストエンジニア・AD/ADAS Application
jobs.description_text: ウーブン・バイ・トヨタについて ウーブン・バイ・トヨタは、トヨタの100年に一度のモビリティ・カンパニーへの変革に寄与していきます。「自分以外の誰かのために」発明を続けたという歴史からインスピレーションを受けた私たちのミッションーそれは、モビリティの定義を拡げ、そしてモビリティが社会に貢献する方法を拡張し、人を想うイノベーションで、モビリティの常識に挑み続けることです。 私たちは4つの柱を中心に活動しています：自動運転・先進運転支援システム技術のAD/ADAS、SDV（ソフトウェア定義車両）のための車両ソフトウェア生産プラットフォームであるArene、モビリティのテストコースであるWoven City、そして協業基盤を支えるデジタル・インフラストラクチャのCloud & AIです。また、ビジネスに不可欠な機能がこれらのチームの実装を下支えし、一丸となって「事故ゼロ社会」と「幸せの量産」の実現に向けて取り組んでいます。 ========================================================================= チームについて Teammate Driving (POV BEV) チームは、自動運転システムにおける最も基本的な機能の1つである車線維持機能と、自動運転システムで使用される地図情報提供サービスを開発しています。テストエンジニアのミッションは、システム要件に基づいて実装されたソフトウェアの機能、性能、品質基準を設定し、評価し、設計者にフィードバックし、製品の性能と品質を向上させることです。また、これらの製品をトヨタの次世代運転支援システム「Toyota Safety Sense」と「Teammate」に実装し、世界中の顧客により安全な運転とより快適なモビリティを提供します。 求める人材 私たちは、ソフトウェアのパフォーマンスと品質を向上させるために、AD/ADAS車両評価の運用と問題分析を行い、問題解決を推進できるエンジニアを探しています。また、ソフトウェアエンジニア、テストドライバ、さまざまな協力者と良好な関係を築くために、新しい価値を提案し、効果的にコミュニケーションできる人材を求めています。尚、定期的に東京・日本橋のオフィスに出社し、静岡県東富士のテストコースで実地試験の実施が必要となります。 業務内容 プロジェクトの進捗状況に合わせた評価計画の策定と管理 システム要件を満たすテストシナリオの作成 実車でのテストと特定された問題の原因の特定 アジャイル開発における問題管理と解決の推進 必須条件 以下のスキルと経験が必要です。 ・技術 ・車両評価業務 ・ユーザー視点でソフトウェア要件が満たされていることを検証する能力 ・Gitによるソフトウェア管理能力 ・AD（自動運転）/ADAS（先進運転支援システム）に関する知識と各技術の相互作用の理解 ・管理 ・優れた問題解決能力、仮説検証能力、タスク管理能力 ・ドキュメンテーション能力 ・さまざまな情報を体系化し、首尾一貫した計画を立案する能力 ・言語 ・日常的な場面で使われる日本語を理解できる能力。（例：日本語能力試験N2以上、または同等のレベル）

Spark is a dedicated team of tenured Client Partners and Client Account Managers who step in to look after a colleague's clients and business while they're on a leave of absence. They safeguard relationships and revenue, keep the work moving, and hand back a healthy, thriving book when our teammate returns. What it means for you . When you take a leave, you can be fully present for what matters — knowing your clients are in expert hands and there's a strong business to come back to, providing the confidence to step away, and the momentum to step back in. Because creating a life you love means being able to step away — and Spark keeps your business thriving while you do. Pinterest's Spark program is a full-time staffing model purpose-built to ensure uninterrupted client service and consistent business performance during periods of extended employee leave, including parental and medical absences. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Command Centre (Frontend & UI/UX)
jobs.description_text: The Role You will build the Command Centre, the screen an operator uses to see what our robots and cameras see, decide in seconds, and task the fleet. Soldiers have already run our console unaided after a short introduction. Next, one operator watches many sites, and tasks robots in plain language instead of drawing routes. That needs an interface built for it. This role is engineering and design in one. You will shape the flows, prototype them, test them with operators, and ship them in production code, working with our full-stack engineer on the backend and our vision engineers on what the models show. What You'll Work On Operator interface: live video, site maps, robot positions and alerts in one view that works at 03:00. Alert triage: the flow from alert to decision: evidence, context, confirm or dismiss, dispatch a robot. Tasking by instruction: an interface for telling the fleet what to do in plain language, and seeing how it plans to do it. Design system: components and patterns that keep the product consistent as it grows. Usability: prototype, test with operators, measure, iterate. Performance: real-time streams and many sites without the interface slowing down. Who We're Looking For A frontend engineer with real UI/UX craft, who has shipped data-heavy, real-time interfaces that people rely on under pressure. Your Background 3+ years of frontend engineering with TypeScript and React. Shipped real-time, data-heavy interfaces: maps, video, dashboards or control panels.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Simulation (Digital Twins)
jobs.description_text: The Role You will be the first engineer on our Simulation team. Every site we map becomes a digital twin, built from our own lidar maps, and in it our robots see thousands of the intrusions, fires and sensor failures a real site sees once a year. Our multi-robot patrol policy was trained in simulation in under two hours on a single GPU and ran unmodified on real robots at three sites. Your job is to make that repeatable for every site and every new skill. You will work with our Skills & Orchestration engineers, who train learned skills with reinforcement learning, and with our Reliability & Test Infrastructure engineer, who runs regression in the same simulator. What You'll Work On Map to twin: a pipeline from our lidar maps to simulation-ready digital twins: geometry, semantics, materials, sensors. Training environments: RL environments for learned skills such as multi-robot patrol and search, randomised so nothing overfits one site. jobs.description_text: The Role You will own the research question at the centre of LEA, our foundation model of the physical world: can a model learn what normally happens on a site, by place, hour and weather, so that an anomaly is simply what it did not expect? The first version is a probabilistic memory of each site. The next is a world model across every site that predicts the next state in latent space, starting from open world-model weights and growing on field data nobody else holds. Our robots and cameras run on live security sites around the clock, and every event is kept with its clip, the model's verdict and the operator's outcome. That record is your dataset. You will work alongside our perception and model engineers, and your results go into production, not only into papers. What You'll Work On Site memory: a learned, probabilistic model of each site: which people, vehicles and robots are where, at what hour, in what weather, and how the scene usually unfolds. Anomaly as surprise: replace rule-based alerting with measured surprise, and work out how to evaluate it when real incidents are rare. World model: post-train open world-model weights on aligned multi-sensor field sequences, JEPA-style, predicting in latent space rather than pixels. Transfer: from one site's memory to a model of all of them, and representations that carry across sites and domains. jobs.description_text: Location: This role is based onsite in Geneva, Switzerland. Travel: Job ID: 1892 ID Quantique (IDQ), part of IonQ, is a global leader in quantum-safe communications. We provide solutions to protect governments, telecommunication infrastructures, and banking & financial institutions from the “harvest-now, decrypt-later” threat, delivering both terrestrial and space-based quantum-safe networks in live operation globally. The Role: We are looking for a Principal Engineer to own the classical cryptography architecture of our post-quantum cryptography (PQC) hardware acceleration products, targeting hardware security module (HSM) and network-appliance applications. Real-world quantum-safe systems are hybrid systems: classical and post-quantum algorithms operating side by side, with careful key management, crypto agility and migration paths. You will be the senior authority for this classical and hybrid layer, working alongside our PQC architecture leadership. The role demands fluency on both sides of the transition: deep classical mastery combined with a solid working command of the post-quantum algorithms and standards the products are built around. Responsibilities : You will own the architecture and implementation strategy of the classical cryptographic functions of the product line: symmetric ciphers and modes (AES/GCM and beyond), hash functions (SHA-2/SHA-3, HMAC/KDF constructions), RSA/ECC offload, and true random number generation and entropy architecture (SP 800-90A/B/C).
